nodes.name: New Ticket Webhook
nodes.notes: POST JSON: { ticket_id, subject, body, requester }. Uses responseNode mode so the caller gets the classification back synchronously and can act on it.

nodes.name: Normalize Ticket
nodes.notes: Truncate the body to 6000 characters here rather than in the prompt. A pasted 40-page log should cost a bounded number of tokens.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({
  model: 'gpt-4o-mini',
  temperature: 0,
  response_format: { type: 'json_object' },
  messages: [
    {
      role: 'system',
      content: [
        'You are a service desk triage assistant for a managed services provider.',
        'Classify the ticket and summarize it for the engineer who will pick it up.',
        '',
        'Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. No markdown, no code fences, no commentary.',
        'The object must have exactly these keys:',
        '  "category": one of "voice", "network", "infrastructure", "other"',
        '  "confidence": a number between 0 and 1',
        '  "summary": exactly three sentences describing the reported problem, its scope, and its urgency',
        '  "first_diagnostic_step": one sentence naming the single first thing the engineer should check',
        '',
        'Category definitions:',
        '  voice          — phones, PBX, SIP trunks, call quality, voicemail, dial plans',
        '  network        — connectivity, routing, switching, wireless, VPN, firewall, DNS, ISP circuits',
        '  infrastructure — servers, virtualization, storage, backups, identity, email systems, endpoints',
        '  other          — billing, scheduling, access requests, or anything not clearly in the three above',
        '',
        'If the ticket is ambiguous, choose the best fit and lower the confidence. Never invent a fifth category.',
        'Do not speculate about causes the ticket text does not support.'
      ].join('\n')
    },
    {
      role: 'user',
      content: 'Subject: ' + $json.subject + '\nRequester: ' + $json.requester + '\n\nBody:\n' + $json.ticket_body
    }
  ]
}) }}

nodes.name: Classify & Summarize
nodes.notes: Attach an "OpenAI-or-compatible API" credential. temperature 0 because triage should be repeatable: the same ticket submitted twice must not land in two different queues.

nodes.name: Parse & Validate JSON
nodes.notes: Validates shape, not just syntax. Anything unparseable or off-schema becomes category "other" with needs_review — degraded, never dropped.

nodes.name: Classifier Unreachable
nodes.notes: A triage endpoint that returns a 500 when the model is down turns one outage into two. This branch keeps the webhook contract intact.

nodes.name: Route by Category
nodes.notes: The fallback output is doing real work here: it catches both genuine "other" tickets and every validation failure from the node before it.

nodes.name: Assign to Voice Queue
nodes.notes: Swap in your ticketing system's assignment endpoint. The summary is written back onto the ticket so the engineer reads it in context, not in a chat message.

nodes.name: Assign to Network Queue
nodes.notes: Swap in your ticketing system's assignment endpoint.

nodes.name: Assign to Infrastructure Queue
nodes.notes: Swap in your ticketing system's assignment endpoint.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ queue: 'triage-review', summary: $json.summary, first_step: $json.first_diagnostic_step, needs_review: true, classifier_error: $json.classifier_error }) }}

nodes.name: Assign to Triage Review
nodes.notes: Genuine "other" tickets and classifier failures both land here. Keeping them in one human-reviewed queue is what makes the automation safe to leave running.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ticket_id: $json.ticket_id, category: $json.category, confidence: $json.confidence, summary: $json.summary, first_diagnostic_step: $json.first_diagnostic_step, needs_review: $json.needs_review }) }}

nodes.name: Respond with Classification
nodes.notes: Always 200, even on a classifier failure — the caller gets category "other" and needs_review true, which is a real answer, not an error to handle.
